_comment: Columns of sand that walk the Age (design 5.2.2). It means the phenomenon outright rather than searching for
for one, which is what `means_exactly` is for and what `VocabularyCheck` insists on: a tag query -- 'the burying
one' -- would also have found whatever else buried you.
`deluge` would be the better word and is deliberately not spent here (Jonah, 2026-08-31). It belongs to
the watery flood, which is not written yet; a word spent on the wrong phenomenon is worse than a
plainer one on the right phenomenon.
**One aspect, and the climate is not touched.** A sandfall wants a dry Age and it is not going to ask
for one here: a rainfall bound in this file would make it a word about the weather as well, and a
second part narrowed is a second part paid for. A writer who wants a desert has `arid`.
